record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: Does every convex body K in R^n admit an ellipsoid E and an absolute constant C such that E captures at least half of its own volume inside K and, after scaling E by a factor C log n, the scaled ellipsoid captures at least half of the volume of K? Equivalently, is there always an ellipsoid E for which vol(E ∩ K) ≥ (1/2) vol(E) and vol(K ∩ C log n E) ≥ (1/2) vol(K)?

evidence.quote:
I Conjecture 5. There exists a constant C such that for any convex body K in R^n, there exists an ellipsoid E that satisfies approximate sandwiching:
vol(E ∩ K) ≥ 1/2 vol(E); vol(K ∩ C log nE) ≥ 1/2 vol(K).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let K ⊂ ℝ^n be a convex body (a compact convex set with non-empty interior). For an ellipsoid E ⊂ ℝ^n and a real number t > 0, denote by tE the dilation of E by factor t about its center, and write vol(·) for n-dimensional Lebesgue measure.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant C > 0 (independent of n and K) such that for every n and every convex body K ⊂ ℝ^n, one can find an ellipsoid E ⊂ ℝ^n satisfying both
  (i) vol(E ∩ K) ≥ (1/2) vol(E), and
  (ii) vol(K ∩ (C log n) E) ≥ (1/2) vol(K).

In other words, must every convex body admit an ellipsoid that contains at least half its own volume inside K, and whose dilate by a factor C log n contains at least half the volume of K?
artifact.status_search_result: The approximate sandwiching conjecture asking for an ellipsoid that captures half its own volume in K and whose C log n dilation captures half of K is stated as a conjecture in Vempala's survey on algorithmic convex geometry. No published resolution was located in the search; related work focuses on M-ellipsoids and isotropic sandwiching at factor n, but a log n approximate sandwiching has not been confirmed or refuted.
